Subject: Geobound contract schedule and subprocessor snapshot

Hi Hannah / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme Health's security team has a few outstanding items before legal will approve the DPA. Two specific asks:

1) Can Redwood provide a concrete timeline and contract language that commits to EU-only processing for our production data with an explicit, limited transient-failover window (we'd prefer < 4 hours, please indicate the maximum bound you can accept).

2) We need a current subprocessor inventory for any services that will touch EU data (including the partner handling network bridges). Please include vendor name, country, and whether they have access to plaintext data or only encrypted blobs.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with our questions (ACME_DPA_Questions.xlsx).

We'd like to resolve these items this week if possible — can we schedule a 30-min call to align on language and timeline?

Best,
Lena Park
Data Protection Officer
Acme Health

--

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.example>

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geobound contract schedule and subprocessor snapshot

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear asks. High-level responses and proposed next steps below, and I attached our residency matrix for reference.

- Commitment: Redwood can contractually commit to processing Acme Health production data within the EU region for the agreed workload. We also support a documented temporary failover window for emergency routing; our standard operational bound is 72 hours but we can discuss a shorter bound for Acme (see legal's note).

- Subprocessors: CloudSync (our network partner) will be in-scope; we maintain a live roster and can provide a snapshot with country-level locations and data access roles. We will confirm access levels (plaintext vs encrypted) for each entry.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa to propose DPA addendum language for a 24-72h transient egress window and required notification windows.
2) KarThik to provide an ops-level runbook describing failover triggers and containment controls (KV-cache isolation, short-lived keys, audit logging).
3) Set a 30-min call tomorrow 09:00 CET to finalize language.

I attached: redwood-residency-matrix.pdf

Happy to hop on a call — available 09:00-11:00 CET tomorrow.

Thanks,
Hannah
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood-residency-matrix.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.example, DPO <dpo@acme.health>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example, partner@cloudsync.io
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geobound contract schedule and subprocessor snapshot

Hi all — quick legal framing and proposed text excerpts. Per Hannah's note, we can do an explicit EU-processing commitment for production data. A few details to confirm before we finalize:

- Failover window: Redwood's operational playbook supports a 72-hour maximum transient failover for rare infrastructure incidents. For customers requiring tighter bounds, we can add an SLA-backed clause limiting transient egress to 24 hours with associated remedies (we'll need to reflect that in pricing).

- Proposed clause (draft): "Redwood shall process Customer Production Data in the EU region. In the event of emergency failover or region outage, Redwood may route transient processing outside of the EU for a maximum period of [X] hours exclusively to preserve service continuity. Redwood will notify Customer within one (1) hour of any failover event and will remediate and return processing to the EU as soon as practicable."

- Subprocessor inventory: please provide a snapshot with vendor, country, purpose, access level, and matrix indicating whether the subprocessor stores or processes plaintext Customer Data. We will attach the inventory as an exhibit.

I've attached a proposed DPA addendum (proposed-dpa-addendum-20270621.docx) with placeholders for the [X] hours and pricing terms. If Acme wants 24h maximum, finance will need to run a quick uplift calculation.

Marissa
Head of Legal
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: proposed-dpa-addendum-20270621.docx (document stub)

From: CloudSync Partner <partner@cloudsync.io>

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:08:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Geobound contract schedule and subprocessor snapshot

Hi Hannah / Marissa — attaching the subprocessor snapshot for the EU environment. Summary below:

- cloudsync-core (DE) — handles network bridging and transient cache replication; encrypted in transit and at rest; no plaintext access.
- sync-ops (IE) — operational support for patching and telemetry; has limited decrypt access for incident triage under dual-control.
- telemetry-analytics (US) — aggregated telemetry export (no identifiers) used for performance tuning, only receives hashed/aggregated data.

Attachment: cloudsync-subprocessors.csv (CSV stub)

Note: We can scope an EU-only deployment for the core bridge and offer an SLA for notification on any planned maintenance that could trigger transient routing. Happy to join the call.

— Elias, CloudSync

--
Attachment: cloudsync-subprocessors.csv (CSV stub)

From: DPO <dpo@acme.health>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.example
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, partner@cloudsync.io
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:15:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Geobound contract schedule and subprocessor snapshot

Thanks for the fast responses and the inventory, Elias. A couple clarifications from Acme:

- The telemetry-analytics entry is acceptable so long as it never receives identifiable patient data. Please confirm the export contains only aggregated, irreversible hashes and cannot be re-identified.

- For sync-ops (IE) we need a description of the dual-control process (who can decrypt, approval workflow, and audit trail).

- On the failover window: Acme is comfortable negotiating 24 hours as a maximum transient egress condition if Redwood includes a one-time onboarding fee and a contractual credit for breaches of that bound. Please confirm commercial uplift and whether Redwood can commit to the notification timing (1 hour).

We can take the 30-min call tomorrow 09:00 CET.

Thanks,
Lena Park
DPO, Acme Health
